steps.name: Map Ensembl zebrafish IDs to symbols and human orthologs

steps.context: Row identifiers come from an Ensembl Danio rerio annotation per the data profile. org.Dr.eg.db (Bioconductor 3.22.0) and babelgene (CRAN 22.9) are both confirmed installed. The reference store was checked: gene-identifier resources cover human, mouse and rat only, and there is no zebrafish GMT in any pathways collection, so ortholog mapping must be done from the installed packages rather than from a staged file.
steps.question: What are the zebrafish gene symbols for the differentially expressed Ensembl IDs, and what fraction of the 12,000 tested genes has a usable human ortholog for cross-species pathway testing?
constraints: Use the installed zebrafish organism annotation package and the installed ortholog package. Do NOT attempt any network lookup — the sandbox has no network.

Preserve the full 12,000-gene tested set in the ranked lists (minus unmappable IDs) — do not truncate to significant genes; GSEA needs the whole ranking.
Report mapping and ortholog rates as explicit numbers, not as prose adjectives.
steps.description: Take the full DESeq2 result table from T1S2 (keyed on Ensembl Danio rerio gene IDs) and build two annotation layers. First, native zebrafish annotation: map Ensembl gene IDs to ZFIN/zebrafish gene symbols and Entrez IDs using the installed zebrafish organism annotation package, reporting the mapping rate and how many IDs are multi-mapped or unmapped. Second, a zebrafish-to-human ortholog map using the installed ortholog package (babelgene), keeping only 1:1 or best-scoring orthologs, and reporting the ortholog coverage rate over both the full tested set and the padj<0.05 subset. Emit three artifacts: (a) the annotated full result table with zebrafish symbol and Entrez appended, (b) a ranked list for native-organism GSEA keyed on zebrafish Entrez ID with the apeglm-shrunken LFC as the ranking statistic, and (c) an ortholog-mapped ranked list keyed on HGNC human symbol, collapsing many-to-one mappings by keeping the entry with the largest absolute shrunken LFC and reporting how many collapses occurred. Zebrafish-to-human ortholog coverage is reported separately for the full tested set and for the padj<0.05 subset
An annotated full result table, a zebrafish-Entrez ranked list, and a human-symbol ranked list are all written to disk
Duplicate collapse rule (largest absolute shrunken LFC wins) is applied and the number of collapsed duplicates is reported

steps.name: Pathway enrichment: native zebrafish GO plus ortholog-mapped human gene sets
caveats: Cross-species enrichment inherits every ortholog-mapping loss from T1S3; if coverage there was low, Arm B results are weakly supported and must be labelled as such.
GO is a nested hierarchy — parent and child terms will co-occur as correlated hits. Collapse redundant terms (or report the redundancy) before quoting a count of enriched processes.

Whole-larvae RNA-seq mixes every tissue, so an enrichment signal may reflect a shift in tissue proportion or developmental stage rather than a cell-intrinsic drug response. Do not claim a mechanism from enrichment alone.
With 3 vs 3 the ranked list is noisy; GSEA NES values will be unstable and near-threshold sets should not be over-interpreted.
steps.context: The reference store was inventoried: it holds MSigDB hallmark (human, mouse), MSigDB GO BP/CC/MF (human, mouse), MSigDB canonical pathways KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID (human only), and WikiPathways (human, mouse, rat). There is NO zebrafish GMT of any kind, which is why native enrichment must come from the org.Dr.eg.db GO annotation via clusterProfiler rather than from a staged gene-set file, and why human gene sets require the T1S3 ortholog bridge.
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are enriched among the genes responding to drug exposure in zebrafish larvae, and do the native-organism GO result and the ortholog-mapped human pathway result agree?
constraints: Use the human gene-set collections ONLY with the ortholog-mapped human-symbol list from T1S3 — never run zebrafish symbols against human GMTs, which fails silently as an empty match rather than erroring.
Never substitute the mouse or rat gene sets for a missing human one, and never use a human GMT as a stand-in for zebrafish annotation in Arm A.
Background universe for over-representation is the set of genes actually tested by DESeq2, not all annotated zebrafish genes — the matrix is already pre-filtered to 12,000 genes.
GSEA parameters: 10,000 permutations, minGSSize 15, maxGSSize 500, BH adjustment applied within each collection separately, and a fixed random seed recorded in the output.
Report q-values, not raw p-values, as the primary significance column in every table.
steps.description:
Run enrichment in two independent arms on the outputs of T1S3 and report them side by side.

Arm A (native, no ortholog assumption): GO over-representation analysis on the padj<0.05 gene set (split into up and down as well as combined) against the zebrafish organism annotation, using the 12,000 tested genes as the background universe rather than the whole genome; and GSEA on the full zebrafish-Entrez ranked list over GO Biological Process. Report BH-adjusted q-values.

Arm B (cross-species): GSEA on the human-symbol ranked list against staged human gene-set collections — the hallmark collection, GO Biological Process, the canonical-pathway collections (KEGG MEDICUS, BioCarta, PID), and human WikiPathways. Resolve each collection from the reference store at run time; if any one collection is absent, skip it, say so, and continue with the rest. Use 10,000 permutations, gene-set size bounds 15-500, and BH adjustment within each collection separately.

Then produce a reconciliation table: for the top enriched terms in Arm B, state whether a semantically matching term also appears in Arm A, and label every Arm-B-only finding as ortholog-dependent. Produce dot plots of the top terms per collection and a GSEA enrichment plot for the top 3 sets. If Arm A's over-representation input has fewer than 10 significant genes, skip ORA, say why, and rely on the GSEA arms.
acceptance_criteria: Arm A produces GO enrichment computed against the zebrafish organism annotation with the 12,000 tested genes as the explicit background universe, not a default genome-wide universe

Arm B runs GSEA against at least the human hallmark and human GO Biological Process collections resolved from the reference store, with any absent collection named and skipped rather than silently dropped
Every enrichment table reports the BH-adjusted q-value, the normalized enrichment score or odds ratio, the gene-set size, and the leading-edge or overlapping genes
A reconciliation table marks each top human-gene-set finding as either corroborated by the native zebrafish GO arm or ortholog-dependent
Dot plots per collection and enrichment plots for the top 3 sets are produced
If no gene set reaches q<0.05 in either arm, the step reports that outcome directly rather than presenting nominal-p results as the headline

plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug-treated vs control DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12,000 genes x 6 samples, gene-level Salmon counts on the Ensembl Danio rerio annotation) plus a 6-row sample table carrying one `condition` column: 3 treated vs 3 control whole-larvae pools, unpaired, single batch. That design fixes the analysis: one two-group negative-binomial contrast, then functional interpretation of the ranked result.

T1S1 loads counts.csv and metadata.csv, verifies that the 6 count columns and the 6 metadata rows agree in identity and order, and runs QC that is genuinely informative at n=3/group: library sizes, detected-gene counts, per-sample correlation, and a VST-based PCA/heatmap to see whether condition separates and whether any pool is an outlier. With three replicates per group, dropping an outlier would leave n=2 and is almost never worth it — so the step reports outliers rather than removing them, and that judgement is passed forward explicitly rather than acted on silently.

T1S2 runs the actual contrast with DESeq2 (treated vs control, control as reference level), independent filtering on, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, and apeglm LFC shrinkage for ranking and plotting. Counts are Salmon-derived gene-level counts and the profile does NOT record whether an average-transcript-length correction was applied; the step must state which assumption it made (raw estimated counts rounded to integers, no offset) because that assumption is not recoverable from the file. n=3 per group is the minimum for dispersion estimation: the step must report the number of genes at FDR<0.05 and, if that number is small, say so plainly instead of relaxing the threshold post hoc.

T1S3 handles the identifier problem that gates all downstream interpretation. The row identifiers come from an Ensembl Danio rerio annotation; org.Dr.eg.db is installed and gives Ensembl->zebrafish symbol/Entrez natively. But the reference store holds NO zebrafish gene sets — WikiPathways is human/mouse/rat only, MSigDB is human/mouse only, and no zebrafish GMT exists here. So the step also builds a zebrafish->human ortholog map (babelgene, installed) so the ranked list can be tested against human gene sets. Both mappings are reported with their coverage rate, because a poor ortholog rate is itself the main caveat on every pathway claim downstream.

T1S4 does the enrichment two ways on purpose. Native-organism GO over-representation and GSEA via clusterProfiler/org.Dr.eg.db needs no ortholog step and is the more trustworthy of the two. Cross-species GSEA of the ortholog-mapped ranked list against the staged human MSigDB hallmark, GO-BP and canonical-pathway (KEGG MEDICUS / BioCarta / PID) GMTs and human WikiPathways gives named, interpretable pathways at the cost of an ortholog assumption. Where the two agree, the pathway call is solid; where only the human-set arm fires, it is flagged as ortholog-dependent. Both use the full shrunk-LFC ranking (GSEA), not just the significant subset, which is what makes the analysis usable even if the FDR<0.05 gene count is small.

steps.context: The reference store was inventoried: it holds MSigDB hallmark (human, mouse), MSigDB GO BP/CC/MF (human, mouse), MSigDB canonical pathways KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID (human only), and WikiPathways (human, mouse, rat). There is NO zebrafish GMT of any kind, which is why native enrichment must come from the org.Dr.eg.db GO annotation via clusterProfiler rather than from a staged gene-set file, and why human gene sets require the T1S3 ortholog bridge.
acceptance_criteria: Arm A produces GO enrichment computed against the zebrafish organism annotation with the 12,000 tested genes as the explicit background universe, not a default genome-wide universe

Arm B runs GSEA against at least the human hallmark and human GO Biological Process collections resolved from the reference store, with any absent collection named and skipped rather than silently dropped
Every enrichment table reports the BH-adjusted q-value, the normalized enrichment score or odds ratio, the gene-set size, and the leading-edge or overlapping genes
A reconciliation table marks each top human-gene-set finding as either corroborated by the native zebrafish GO arm or ortholog-dependent
Dot plots per collection and enrichment plots for the top 3 sets are produced
If no gene set reaches q<0.05 in either arm, the step reports that outcome directly rather than presenting nominal-p results as the headline
constraints: Use the human gene-set collections ONLY with the ortholog-mapped human-symbol list from T1S3 — never run zebrafish symbols against human GMTs, which fails silently as an empty match rather than erroring.
Never substitute the mouse or rat gene sets for a missing human one, and never use a human GMT as a stand-in for zebrafish annotation in Arm A.
Background universe for over-representation is the set of genes actually tested by DESeq2, not all annotated zebrafish genes — the matrix is already pre-filtered to 12,000 genes.
GSEA parameters: 10,000 permutations, minGSSize 15, maxGSSize 500, BH adjustment applied within each collection separately, and a fixed random seed recorded in the output.
Report q-values, not raw p-values, as the primary significance column in every table.
caveats: Cross-species enrichment inherits every ortholog-mapping loss from T1S3; if coverage there was low, Arm B results are weakly supported and must be labelled as such.
GO is a nested hierarchy — parent and child terms will co-occur as correlated hits. Collapse redundant terms (or report the redundancy) before quoting a count of enriched processes.

Whole-larvae RNA-seq mixes every tissue, so an enrichment signal may reflect a shift in tissue proportion or developmental stage rather than a cell-intrinsic drug response. Do not claim a mechanism from enrichment alone.
With 3 vs 3 the ranked list is noisy; GSEA NES values will be unstable and near-threshold sets should not be over-interpreted.
